title: Fitting an extractor duct liner through a cavity wall
subtitle: Core-drill through a cavity wall and fit a sleeve liner and external vent grille for a kitchen or bathroom extractor fan
excerpt: How to fit a duct liner through a cavity wall to duct a kitchen or bathroom extractor fan to the outside. Covers core-drilling through the inner leaf, cavity, and outer leaf, fitting the liner sleeve, and fixing the external grille.
sourceNotes: Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). Black and Decker Complete Photo Guide to Home Improvement (referenced, not reproduced). UK Building Regulations Part F guidance on ventilation (open access).

glossaryTerms.definition: A rigid PVC or aluminium sleeve (typically 100 mm or 125 mm diameter) fitted through a cavity wall to create a clean passage for an extractor duct. The liner bridges the inner leaf, the cavity, and the outer leaf. Available in standard and adjustable lengths.

A hollow circular drill bit attached to an SDS plus or SDS max drill, used to cut a clean circular hole through masonry or brick. Sizes from 50 mm to 200 mm diameter. The most controlled method for cutting a duct hole; less damage to the surrounding masonry than chasing and chiselling.

content.text: Ducting an extractor fan through a
means drilling a clean hole through two leaves of masonry with a

, fitting a rigid liner sleeve through the hole, and fixing an external louvred grille. The liner keeps the duct clean and prevents the cavity from becoming the duct passage. A 100 mm diameter duct suits most domestic extractors; 125 mm is used for higher-powered range hoods.

Sweep a cable-and-pipe detector across the wall in the line of the proposed hole on both the inside and outside faces. Mark any hit with pencil. The duct position must clear any gas pipes (marked in yellow) and any buried electrical cable. Choose a position that clears all services. Check the cavity for cavity-wall insulation by drilling a small inspection hole first; insulation slows the core drilling and falls into the cavity on completion.
Mark and drill the inner leaf

Mark the centre of the duct hole on the inside wall. The hole must slope very slightly toward the outside (about 2-3 degrees) so condensation drains outward. Fit the core drill bit to the SDS drill. Start slow; set the bit position with the drill running at low speed before pressing to full pressure. Drill through the inner leaf only (typically 100-105 mm for a 100 mm brick course plus plaster), then stop. Probe the cavity with a piece of stiff wire to check the route is clear.
Drill the outer leaf and fit the liner

Move outside. Find the centre of the hole in the outer leaf using a long drill bit passed through the inner hole to mark the outer face. Core-drill through the outer leaf at the same slight downward slope. Clean away the core and any rubble from the cavity. Slide the liner sleeve through from the outside; the sleeve should protrude 25-30 mm on each face for the duct connections. Make good the gap between the sleeve and the brick on both faces with exterior-grade mortar or fire-rated sealant.

The external louvred grille snaps or screws onto the outer end of the liner. Most grilles include a back-draught flap that opens when the fan is running and closes when it is off. Fix the grille flange to the outer wall face with stainless steel screws and make good the perimeter joint with exterior-grade silicone sealant. Connect the extractor fan duct to the inner end of the liner and seal with duct tape or a duct connector.

attrs.symptom: Condensation drips inside the duct and back into the fan
attrs.cause: The duct slopes inward (toward the fan) rather than outward.
attrs.fix: Refit the liner with a slight outward slope. Insulating the duct through the cavity also reduces condensation in cold weather.

attrs.symptom: Cold air enters the room when the fan is off
attrs.cause: The back-draught flap on the external grille is sticking open or is missing.
attrs.fix: Clean the flap hinge; if corroded or broken, replace the grille with a model that has a spring-loaded flap.
